name: Performance Marketing
summary: A D2C brand with a budget cut, over-claiming ad dashboards and an agency plan with flaws that only show up if you do the unit economics.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: First read
stages.summary: Read the channel table and say what worries them most. Think aloud: shows whether they spot over-attribution and unit economics.

stages.title: The budget cut
stages.summary: Commit to where a budget cut comes from and estimate the impact on orders. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two weeks later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their cut. Tests whether they update on new data and explain why it happened.

stages.title: Critique the agency's plan
stages.summary: Critique an agency plan with planted flaws, including a target ROAS below break-even. Think aloud.

stages.title: Founder update (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a founder update with any AI tool and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI, not just whether they use it.

stages.title: A real decision
stages.summary: A real budget or channel decision from their career that didn't go to plan. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Content & Brand Marketing
summary: A B2B SaaS blog whose traffic doubled while trials stayed flat, a quarter's content bet, and a content brief that contradicts the customer research.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Traffic up, trials flat
stages.summary: Explain to the CEO why traffic doubled but trials did not. Think aloud: shows whether they judge content by intent, not volume.

stages.title: Next quarter's bet
stages.summary: Commit to how the next quarter's 12 pieces are spent and estimate the trial impact. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two months later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their bet. Tests whether they adapt and explain what happened.

stages.title: Review a freelancer's brief
stages.summary: Critique a content brief that contradicts the customer research and makes a false pricing claim. Think aloud.

stages.title: Positioning (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the comparison page positioning and headlines with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real piece of content
stages.summary: A real piece of content or campaign that didn't move the business metric. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: SEO
summary: An organic revenue drop after a site migration, with a Google core update as a red herring, a recovery plan, and an agency audit that would make things worse.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What caused the drop?
stages.summary: Diagnose the organic drop and separate the migration from the core update. Think aloud: shows whether they reason from evidence or from the news.

stages.title: The recovery plan
stages.summary: Choose the main fix for the next sprint and estimate the recovery. Think aloud: shows prioritisation under engineering constraints.

stages.title: Three weeks later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their plan. Tests whether they adapt and own the result.

stages.title: Review the agency's audit
stages.summary: Critique an agency audit whose recommendations would block the new category pages from Google. Think aloud.

stages.title: CEO update and redirect ticket (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the CEO update and the engineering ticket for the redirects with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real SEO change
stages.summary: A real SEO change they made or recommended that didn't work. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Social Media
summary: Engagement that is "up" because of a giveaway whose followers leave, a plan for the next quarter, and a public reply to a viral complaint that would make it worse.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What is actually working?
stages.summary: Explain what the engagement numbers hide and what actually drives sales. Think aloud: shows whether they look past vanity metrics.

stages.title: Next quarter's plan
stages.summary: Commit to where the quarter's budget goes and estimate the sales impact. Think aloud.

stages.title: Six weeks later
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their plan. Tests whether they adapt and explain what happened.

stages.title: Review a reply to a viral complaint
stages.summary: Critique an intern's public reply to a viral complaint that exposes the customer's details and makes things worse. Think aloud.

stages.title: Reel captions (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write on-brand Reel hooks and captions with any AI tool, and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI.

stages.title: A real campaign or post
stages.summary: A real social campaign or post that got attention but didn't help the business. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Customer Support Leadership
summary: The morning after a payment outage: a backlog capacity alone cannot clear, a tempting shortcut, and a draft reply with a serious security mistake in it.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: The first 30 minutes
stages.summary: Read the outage dashboard and say what to do first. Think aloud: shows whether they go after demand or just add effort.

stages.title: One lever
stages.summary: Commit to one lever (proactive message, overtime, bulk-close, borrowed staff) and estimate the end-of-day backlog. Think aloud.

stages.title: Midday
stages.summary: The situation changes based on their lever. Tests whether they adapt and own the downside.

stages.title: Review a new agent's reply
stages.summary: Critique a draft reply with a planted security mistake (asking for an OTP) and a false refund promise. Think aloud.

stages.title: Agent guidance (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write agent guidance with any AI tool and paste the conversation. Shows how they work with AI, not just whether they use it.

stages.title: A real escalation
stages.summary: A real situation from their career that got worse before it got better. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Sales Development (SDR / BDR)
summary: Behind on meetings with two weeks left: pick the right leads from a list full of traps, choose one outbound play, and fix a teammate’s cold email that gets the prospect’s funding round wrong.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Who do you go after first?
stages.summary: Pick three leads from a list with traps in it (a famous logo out of reach, an intern who opens every email). Think aloud.

stages.title: One play for the rest of the month
stages.summary: Choose one outbound play and estimate the qualified meetings it brings. Tests pipeline maths: no single play closes the gap. Think aloud.

stages.title: Four days later
stages.summary: What happens next depends on their play. Tests whether they adjust or keep pushing.

stages.title: Fix a teammate's cold email
stages.summary: A cold email with a wrong fact about the prospect, a too-big ask and an unauthorised discount. Think aloud.

stages.title: A three-touch sequence (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a short sequence for one lead with AI. Catches invented proof points and generic copy.

stages.title: A meeting from a cold start
stages.summary: A real meeting or deal they created from nothing. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Account Executive (B2B)
summary: A deal stuck for two months with the quarter ending: diagnose what is really wrong, decide on a 25% discount request, and catch the errors in a proposal before it goes out.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What's really wrong with this deal?
stages.summary: Diagnose a stalled deal: single-threaded, no economic buyer, a stuck security review, an unrealistic close date. Think aloud.

stages.title: The 25% request
stages.summary: Respond to a discount request above their authority, with quota pressure. Tests deal judgement and maths. Think aloud.

stages.title: A week later
stages.summary: The response to their choice comes back. Tests whether they adapt without panicking.

stages.title: Check the proposal before it goes out
stages.summary: A proposal with the wrong user count, a calculation error and the wrong payment terms. Tests attention to numbers. Think aloud.

stages.title: Email to the CFO (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a short business case email to the CFO with AI. Catches invented ROI numbers.

stages.title: A deal you saved or lost
stages.summary: A real deal that went sideways. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Customer Support Executive
summary: The start of a shift with a mixed queue: spot the safety and fraud tickets under the shouting, handle a refund request outside policy, and fix a teammate’s reply that leaks another customer’s details.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Which tickets first?
stages.summary: Order a mixed queue: safety and fraud tickets hidden among loud but low-risk ones, and one close to breaching its deadline. Think aloud.

stages.title: A return after the window
stages.summary: A loyal customer asks for a refund two days past the return window. Tests policy judgement and authority. Think aloud.

stages.title: The customer replies
stages.summary: The customer reacts to their choice. Tests calm, follow-through and honesty.

stages.title: Check a teammate's reply
stages.summary: A reply that leaks another customer's details, promises the wrong refund time and blames the courier. Think aloud.

stages.title: Reply to a long complaint (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Answer a multi-issue complaint with AI. Catches over-promising and padded apologies.

stages.title: A difficult customer
stages.summary: A real difficult customer they handled. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Product Manager
summary: Retention dropped after a release and the CEO wants a feature for a big customer: find the real cause in the data, decide what the team builds next, and catch the holes in a junior PM’s spec.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Why is retention down?
stages.summary: Find the cause of a retention drop hidden in the averages: Android new users after a sign-up change, with OTP tickets spiking. Think aloud.

stages.title: What gets built next
stages.summary: Choose how to spend six engineer-weeks with the CEO pushing for a customer feature. Think aloud.

stages.title: Three weeks in
stages.summary: Their plan meets reality. Tests adapting and stakeholder management.

stages.title: Review a junior PM's spec
stages.summary: A one-page spec with a vanity success metric, no segment, scope creep and no rollout plan. Think aloud.

stages.title: Update to the CEO (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the cycle plan update to the CEO with AI. Catches vague trade-offs and invented numbers.

stages.title: A product call you got wrong
stages.summary: A real product decision that did not work. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Product Analyst / Associate PM
summary: An A/B test the PM wants to ship on Monday: spot the broken user split and the revenue the headline hides, decide what to recommend, and catch a correlation passed off as cause.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Is this a win?
stages.summary: Read an A/B test with a broken 50/50 split, revenue per user that falls, and a short test over a sale weekend. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your recommendation
stages.summary: Commit to a recommendation with the PM pushing to ship. Think aloud.

stages.title: What happens next
stages.summary: The consequences of their recommendation. Tests adapting and owning the call.

stages.title: Review a teammate's analysis
stages.summary: An analysis that treats a correlation as cause, uses a skewed average and a misleading chart. Think aloud.

stages.title: Write the readout (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the experiment readout for the PM with AI. Catches over-claiming from a p-value.

stages.title: An analysis that changed a decision
stages.summary: A real analysis that changed what a team did. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: UX / Product Designer
summary: A checkout losing a third of users at one step: find the problem from funnel data and usability notes, pick the fix that fits two weeks, and catch the accessibility problems in a proposed screen.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where is checkout breaking?
stages.summary: Use funnel data, usability notes and a heatmap to find the real problem: the address step, for specific reasons. Think aloud.

stages.title: What fits in two weeks
stages.summary: Choose a fix for one engineer for two weeks. Tests scoping to the evidence. Think aloud.

stages.title: After launch
stages.summary: Results of their choice arrive. Tests reading results and adapting.

stages.title: Review a proposed screen
stages.summary: A new address screen spec with placeholder-only labels, colour-only errors, small tap targets and low contrast. Think aloud.

stages.title: Error messages (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the address-form error messages with AI. Catches vague, blaming copy.

stages.title: A design you changed after testing
stages.summary: A real design they changed after seeing users struggle. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Data Analyst
summary: A VP needs "which region grew most" for a board deck in an hour: find the double-loaded month and the cancelled order that flip the answer, decide what to send, and catch the maths mistakes in a teammate’s summary.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Which region grew most?
stages.summary: Answer a VP's question from a dashboard with a double-loaded month and a cancelled order that flip the answer. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you send at 3 pm?
stages.summary: The VP needs a number for the board now; one fix isn't confirmed. Tests judgement under time pressure. Think aloud.

stages.title: The next morning
stages.summary: Consequences of what they sent. Tests ownership and fixing the root cause.

stages.title: Check a teammate's summary
stages.summary: A summary with an average of averages, percent confused with percentage points, and a 14-slice pie chart. Think aloud.

stages.title: The note to the VP (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the corrected regional summary with AI. Catches copied dashboard numbers and false precision.

stages.title: When the data was wrong
stages.summary: A real time they found or missed a data problem. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Business Analyst
summary: Three senior stakeholders want things that can’t all be true: spot the conflict hiding in their numbers, propose a design they can agree on, and fix requirements that no one could test.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where do the requirements clash?
stages.summary: Find the conflict hidden in three stakeholders' numbers (demand far above manual capacity) and the questions to ask. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your proposal
stages.summary: Propose a design all three can sign. Tests trade-offs and quantifying them. Think aloud.

stages.title: The sign-off meeting
stages.summary: A stakeholder pushes back on their proposal. Tests facilitation and adapting.

stages.title: Review the draft requirements
stages.summary: Requirements that are vague, untestable and contradict each other. Think aloud.

stages.title: User stories (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write user stories with acceptance criteria using AI. Catches untestable criteria and invented requirements.

stages.title: Stakeholders who disagreed
stages.summary: A real time they brought conflicting stakeholders to a decision. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: IT Support / Helpdesk
summary: Monday 9 am: a phishing email someone typed their password into, a VPN outage and the CEO’s board meeting. Triage it, contain the phishing, and catch the hole in the password reset process.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Monday 9 am
stages.summary: Order a queue with a security incident, an outage for remote staff and the CEO's deadline. Think aloud.

stages.title: The phishing email
stages.summary: Choose how to respond to a phishing incident with one password entered. Think aloud.

stages.title: An hour later
stages.summary: What their response led to. Tests adapting during an incident.

stages.title: Review the password reset process
stages.summary: A phone reset process that verifies people with public information and reads passwords aloud. Think aloud.

stages.title: VPN outage update (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the staff update about the VPN outage with AI. Catches jargon and invented fix times.

stages.title: An incident you handled
stages.summary: A real outage or security problem they handled. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Operations Manager
summary: One warehouse keeps missing dispatch deadlines and festival week is ten days away: find the real bottleneck (not headcount), plan for the spike, and fix a staffing plan built on wrong assumptions.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Why is one site always late?
stages.summary: Find the real bottleneck at the late site: a late inbound truck that shortens pick time, not too few people. Think aloud.

stages.title: Festival week plan
stages.summary: Choose a plan for a big order spike in ten days. Tests capacity planning and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Festival week, day two
stages.summary: What their plan led to. Tests adapting under pressure.

stages.title: Check the staffing plan
stages.summary: A staffing plan that uses the best site's speed everywhere, ignores breaks and absence, and counts temps as experienced. Think aloud.

stages.title: The shift brief (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the festival-week brief for site supervisors with AI. Catches generic advice and invented numbers.

stages.title: A process you fixed
stages.summary: A real operational problem they fixed. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Project Manager
summary: A client system launch three weeks behind, tied to a big event: find the critical path problem, choose how to recover, and fix a status report that says “green” while the project slips.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Are we on track?
stages.summary: Work out the real status from a dependency chain: the client's late data export pushes go-live out. Think aloud.

stages.title: The recovery plan
stages.summary: Choose a recovery option. Tests trade-offs between scope, time, people and quality. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two weeks later
stages.summary: What their recovery plan led to. Tests adapting and managing the client.

stages.title: Review last week's status report
stages.summary: A "green" status report that hides a slipping dependency, with vague risks and no owners. Think aloud.

stages.title: Email to the sponsor (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the honest re-plan email to the client sponsor with AI. Catches vague dates and blame.

stages.title: A project that slipped
stages.summary: A real project that went off track. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Founder's Office / Chief of Staff
summary: The board meets in three days and every team says its numbers look great: find the growth that is losing money on each order, pick one priority for next quarter, and fix a cherry-picked board slide.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: The three numbers that matter
stages.summary: Pull the real story from four teams' numbers: growth bought with discounts, money lost per order, a shrinking runway. Think aloud.

stages.title: One priority for next quarter
stages.summary: Recommend one company priority. Tests judgement with cash at stake. Think aloud.

stages.title: After the board meeting
stages.summary: Reactions to their priority. Tests adapting and handling people.

stages.title: Review marketing's board slide
stages.summary: A board slide with an inflated CAC claim, revenue without returns and no comparison point. Think aloud.

stages.title: The board note (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the CEO's one-page board note with AI. Catches spin and invented numbers.

stages.title: Something you drove across teams
stages.summary: A real piece of work they drove across teams without authority. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Financial Analyst (FP&A)
summary: Profit beat the budget, so the CEO is happy, but revenue missed: split the miss into price and volume, see that the cost savings are only timing, reforecast the year, and catch the errors in a junior’s reforecast.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Was it really a good quarter?
stages.summary: Explain a profit beat that hides a revenue miss: split price and volume, and see the cost savings are timing. Think aloud.

stages.title: Reforecast the year
stages.summary: Choose how to reforecast after the quarter. Tests forecasting judgement. Think aloud.

stages.title: The CFO and CEO react
stages.summary: Pushback on their reforecast. Tests holding a position with numbers.

stages.title: Check a junior's reforecast
stages.summary: A reforecast that annualises a quarter with a one-off deal in it, mislabels a variance and drops the delayed costs. Think aloud.

stages.title: Board pack commentary (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the quarter commentary for the board pack with AI. Catches spin and arithmetic errors.

stages.title: A forecast that missed
stages.summary: A real forecast or budget that turned out wrong. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Accountant (AP / AR)
summary: Month-end close: reconcile the bank against the books, spot a supplier paid twice, decide how to handle that supplier’s next invoice, and fix a collection email that would anger a good customer.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Reconcile the bank
stages.summary: Match a bank statement against the books: an uncleared cheque, unbooked charges, a receipt keyed twice and one not booked; plus a supplier paid twice. Think aloud.

stages.title: The supplier calls
stages.summary: A key supplier paid twice wants their next invoice paid in full. Tests judgement and firmness. Think aloud.

stages.title: The following week
stages.summary: What their choice led to. Tests follow-through and ownership.

stages.title: Check a collection email
stages.summary: A collection email that threatens legal action, asks for an invoice already paid and gives no invoice details. Think aloud.

stages.title: A payment reminder (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a firm, polite reminder with AI. Catches invented late fees and legal threats.

stages.title: An error you found
stages.summary: A real accounting error they found or fixed. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Equity Research Analyst
summary: A fast-growing listed company that looks cheap: find the red flags in its cash flow, receivables and promoter pledges, make a call, and fix a junior’s valuation built on a one-off gain.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What worries you?
stages.summary: Read four years of numbers: profits growing while cash flow vanishes, receivables doubling, rising related-party sales and pledges. Think aloud.

stages.title: Your recommendation
stages.summary: Make a call on a cheap stock with red flags. Think aloud.

stages.title: A month later
stages.summary: Events after their call. Tests updating views honestly.

stages.title: Check a junior's valuation
stages.summary: A valuation built on a one-off gain, a mismatched peer and ignored dilution. Think aloud.

stages.title: The investment note (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the summary note for the fund manager with AI. Catches hype and invented figures.

stages.title: A call you got wrong
stages.summary: A real investment or analytical call that went wrong. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: HR Business Partner
summary: Attrition is up and the business head wants a 10% raise for everyone: find the one team and manager behind it, choose a fix, and catch the confidentiality breach in a new policy.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: What is really driving attrition?
stages.summary: Find that attrition is concentrated in one team under a new manager, with workload spiralling, not a company-wide pay problem. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you recommend?
stages.summary: Recommend a fix to the business head. Tests judgement, fairness and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Six weeks later
stages.summary: Consequences of their recommendation. Tests adapting and handling people.

stages.title: Review a new policy draft
stages.summary: A policy that shares named exit interview comments with managers and punishes all exits. Think aloud.

stages.title: Talking points for the manager (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Prepare a hard conversation with the manager using AI. Catches vague or accusatory scripts.

stages.title: A people problem you solved
stages.summary: A real people issue they handled. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Recruiter / Talent Acquisition
summary: A hiring manager wants a unicorn on a tight budget: shortlist from eight profiles with traps (big brands, a career break, an explained job-hopper), push back with market data, and fix an outreach message that gets the candidate’s name wrong.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Who goes on the shortlist?
stages.summary: Shortlist three of eight profiles, seeing past brand names and degrees, not penalising a career break or an explained job-hopper. Think aloud.

stages.title: The hiring manager's must-haves
stages.summary: Handle a hiring manager whose must-haves don't fit the budget or market. Think aloud.

stages.title: Three weeks later
stages.summary: What their approach led to. Tests adapting and owning the hiring outcome.

stages.title: Check an outreach message
stages.summary: An outreach message with the wrong name, a generic pitch and an upfront salary question. Think aloud.

stages.title: The job advert (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the job advert with AI. Catches biased wording and inflated requirements.

stages.title: A hard hire
stages.summary: A real hard-to-fill role they closed. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Learning & Development Manager
summary: The CEO wants leadership training for every manager: find the real skill gap in the survey data, design something that changes behaviour within budget, and catch a training report that measures only happiness.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where is the real gap?
stages.summary: Find the real need in survey data: new managers giving feedback (a big gap between self and team ratings), linked to attrition. Think aloud.

stages.title: What do you build?
stages.summary: Choose an approach within budget. Tests design for behaviour change and cost. Think aloud.

stages.title: Halfway through
stages.summary: Their programme meets reality. Tests adapting.

stages.title: Review a training report
stages.summary: A report that claims success from satisfaction scores and a same-day test. Think aloud.

stages.title: Programme outline (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Design a short programme outline with AI. Catches generic content-heavy designs.

stages.title: Training that changed behaviour
stages.summary: A real learning programme and its results. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Product Marketing Manager
summary: A competitor launches a cheaper plan just before your feature launch: find where you really win in the win/loss data, choose the launch message, and cut the unprovable claims from a launch page.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Where do we actually win?
stages.summary: Read win/loss data: the product wins mid-size deals on speed, not features, and loses large deals on security. Think aloud.

stages.title: The launch message
stages.summary: Choose the launch message after a competitor price cut. Think aloud.

stages.title: Two weeks after launch
stages.summary: Results of their message. Tests reading signals and adapting.

stages.title: Review the launch page draft
stages.summary: A launch page with unprovable claims, feature-first copy and the wrong audience. Think aloud.

stages.title: Launch email (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the launch email to customers and prospects with AI. Catches buzzwords and unprovable claims.

stages.title: A launch you ran
stages.summary: A real launch or positioning change. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Influencer & Community Manager
summary: Pick creators for a launch from a list where the biggest account has bought followers, spend the budget for real reach, and fix a creator brief with no ad disclosure and a health claim you can’t make.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Which creators are real value?
stages.summary: Spot bought followers (huge account, low views, foreign audience, sudden growth) and a brand-safety risk; work out real reach per rupee. Think aloud.

stages.title: Spend the budget
stages.summary: Allocate the launch budget across creators. Think aloud.

stages.title: Campaign week
stages.summary: What happens during the campaign. Tests adapting and brand safety.

stages.title: Check the creator brief
stages.summary: A creator brief with no ad disclosure, a claim you can't make and a word-for-word script. Think aloud.

stages.title: Write the creator brief (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write a proper creator brief with AI. Catches invented claims and missing disclosure.

stages.title: A campaign or community you built
stages.summary: A real creator campaign or community effort. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Copywriter / Content Writer
summary: A launch brief with real customer research: find the insight competitors miss, handle a client who wants an unprovable “No. 1” claim, and edit a weak landing page.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Three headline directions
stages.summary: Write three headline directions from the research and pick one. Tests finding the insight competitors miss. Think aloud.

stages.title: The client's "No. 1" line
stages.summary: The client insists on an unprovable superlative. Tests judgement with a client. Think aloud.

stages.title: After it goes live
stages.summary: Consequences of their choice. Tests adapting and ownership.

stages.title: Edit a weak landing page
stages.summary: A draft with jargon, a buried benefit, an unsupported claim and inconsistent voice. Think aloud.

stages.title: Search ads (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write search ad variations with AI within character limits. Catches limits broken and invented claims.

stages.title: Copy that worked (or didn't)
stages.summary: Real writing they did and its results. Checks specificity and ownership.

name: Social Media Executive
summary: Plan next week’s posts from last month’s numbers (trend reels get reach but no clicks), handle a customer complaint going viral, and fix captions with a price typo and a competitor’s hashtag.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Plan next week
stages.summary: Plan posts toward a clicks goal: trend reels win reach but bring almost no clicks; carousels and link stories drive them. Think aloud.

stages.title: A complaint goes viral
stages.summary: A customer's complaint post about the brand is spreading. Choose a response. Think aloud.

stages.title: The next day
stages.summary: What happened after their response. Tests adapting.

stages.title: Check the week's captions
stages.summary: Captions with a price typo, a competitor's hashtag and a joke during a tragedy in the news. Think aloud.

stages.title: Carousel captions (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write captions for the week's carousels with AI. Catches generic copy and hashtag stuffing.

stages.title: A post or page you grew
stages.summary: A real social media result they drove. Checks specificity and ownership.
